newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends up as Refco Inc, Continental buy.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends up as Refco Inc, Continental buy.

text.p: Late buying by Refco Inc and Continental Grain boosted CBOT wheat futures to a higher close, traders said.
Refco bought two million to three million bushels each of May and July and Continental bought one million bushels of July, traders said.

Recent strong stopping of deliveries on the March and persistent talk about damage to portions of the U.S. soft red winter wheat crop due to heavy rains and flooding led to the advances, sources said.
The wheat close ran counter to the late sag in soy.
"There may have been a little wheat/bean spreading but it was real light," a trader said.

USDA's March Supply/Demand report released early Tuesday showed no change in the government's outlook for 1996-97 U.S. wheat ending stocks at 474 million bushels. The estimate remained above the extremely tight stocks tally of 376 million bushels for the 1995-96 marketing year.
Talk of a sale of Canadian wheat to Brazil was largely shrugged off by the market.
Wheat closed 2-1/2 to 6-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with March up 4-1/2 at $3.81 a bushel.
The Canadian Wheat Board overnight sold Brazil up to 600,000 tonnes of milling wheat, grain trade sources in Winnipeg said.

Traders saw few surprises in the government's world production figures with USDA's prediction for Australia's wheat crop at 23.5 million tonnes during 1996-97, which was above the February outlook for 23.1 million but still within expectations.
The Argentine crop estimate was left unchanged at 15.5 million tonnes.

Technicians cited first resistance in the March at $3.80-1/2 and second resistance was at $3.89. The session high for March was $3.81. First support was at $3.68-1/2 and second support was at $3.56. The session low was $3.70.

The four- and 20-day moving averages were giving off bullish signals early Tuesday. The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) in the March closed at 66 percent. The market generally considers an RSI of 70 or more as overbought and 30 or less as oversold.
In addition to late purchases by Refco and Continental, on the day Rosenthal Collins bought two million bushels of July and Tenco Inc bought 1.5 million July, traders said.
Wheat futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 13,000 contracts, above 12,638 traded Monday.
In wheat options, Cargill Investor Services bought 200 May $3.80 calls at 10-1/2 cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 4,000 contracts, above the 3,242 traded Monday.
